sentences.text: 1. Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned AGA and perused the record.

2. The FIR in question was lodged after about four months of the incident on 26.02.2023 through an application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C., alleging that the entire family members of the applicant used to demand dowry and used to harass the daughter of the informant and ultimately, the daughter of the informant died by committing suicide.
It was alleged that the entire family tried to somehow conceal the body with an intent to avoid detection.
Rasheed vs State Of U.P. Thru.

1 3. Learned counsel for the applicant draws my attention to the inquest report, which demonstrates that the inquest was carried out on the information of the applicant, who is the husband.
He further draws my attention to the post-mortem report, which is on record, which reveals the death on account of ante-mortem hanging.
The injuries on the body are ligature mark and apart form the said, no injury has been noticed on the body in question.
The applicant is the husband of the deceased and has been implicated under Section 304B IPC.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant further argues that the FIR in question was lodged after four months of the alleged incident.

The version of the FIR in not corroborated with the inquest report and the post-mortem report, no visible injuries are seen on the body except a ligature mark, and prima-facie the material for alleging that immediately prior to the death, the deceased was subjected to mental and physical torture in relation to demand of dowry, are missing.
The applicant has no criminal antecedent and is in custody since 05.04.2023.

5. Learned AGA opposes the bail application by arguing that the death occurred within two years of the marriage and thus, the presumption under Section 304B IPC will apply against the applicant,
who is the husband of the deceased.
He, thus, argues that the bail application should be rejected.
6. Considering the submissions made at the Bar, prima-facie, the FIR which was lodged after four months does not stand corroborated with the inquest report and the post-mortem report.

The injuries depicted on the body apart from the ligature mark are absent as there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the victim was subjected to death immediately prior to the death on account of the demand of dowry.
The presumption under Section 304B IPC is to be established at the time of trial.
There being nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant, if enlarged on bail, can in any way adversely affect the trial, the applicant is entitled to be enlarged on bail.
In view thereof, the application is allowed.

7. Let the applicant Rasheed be released on bail in FIR No.0092 of 2023, under Section 498A, 304B IPC & Section 3/4 of Dowry Prohibition Act, P.S. Paraspur, District Gonda on his furnishing a personal bond with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of court concerned with the following conditions:
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
